formal_record.question:
Nine points numbered 1 to 9 are marked on a circle. Join point 1 to point 3, then point 3 to point 5, and continue by joining every second point until returning to point 1. Which drawing results?
Choices:
A:(A)
B:(B)
C:(C)
D:(D)
E:(E)

mechanism: The five odd-numbered source points are a red subgroup, paired with the same five vertices in B. B is exactly the closed cycle on that subgroup. This privileges the false interpretation of every second point as odd labels only, incorrectly closing 9 to1 instead of wrapping 9 to2 on the nine-point circle. Every colored point belongs to one end of this source-to-result subgroup correspondence; no route or optionletter is colored.
mathematical_solution: The increment is2 modulo9, so the ordered labels are1,3,5,7,9,2,4,6,8,1. Since gcd(2,9)=1 all nine points are visited and only E has these nine edges. B closes9 directly to1 and omits the even labels, violating the cyclic every-second-point rule. Colors add no vertices and no condition; all markers exactly coincide with existing labeled source/B vertices.
marker_roles: For each n in1,3,5,7,9, source p0_n is colored at its exact original coordinate to encode membership in the tempting odd-label partition.
For each same n, option-B p2_n is colored at its exact original coordinate to bind that member to B's odd-only closed path.
Ten point overlays jointly encode the specific false subgroup correspondence. All54 original points, numberlabels and all original edges remain in place; no new distinct point is added.
human_gate: Each newpoint is centered exactly on one existing point, so the nine-point source and all options retain the same distinct vertices. Every numeral, including9 and2 at the wrap, is unchanged and unobscured. The original black route and circle contours remain readable.
